start: Think of `required` as a debt: `"AAC"` owes two `A`s and one `C`. Each character that enters the window pays back one copy, if that character is still owed; a third `A` pays nothing, and that is allowed. The window covers once nothing is owed.

Grow the window one character at a time with `right`. Whenever nothing is owed, it covers: record it, then shrink it from `left`, recording as you go, until it stops covering. Keep a dict of copies still owed per character, where below zero means surplus, and a total `missing` of owed copies, so covering is `missing == 0` rather than a scan of the dict.

start.text: The shape, with the bookkeeping left to you:

test_examples_and_ties: `("ABAAC", "AAC")` gives `(2, 5)`, `("abxba", "ab")` gives `(0, 2)`, the first of two tied windows, `("ab", "aa")` gives `None`, `("", "")` gives `(0, 0)` and `("🙂x🙂é", "🙂é")` gives `(2, 4)`. `("abc", None)` must raise `ValueError`.

`(3, 5)` for `"ABAAC"` means `required` was treated as a set: it needs two `A`s. `(3, 5)` for `"abxba"` means an equal-length window replaced the first: replace only when strictly shorter. `None` as `required` slips past `if not required:` and `Counter(None)`, so test `isinstance(required, str)` first.
test_all_substrings_oracle: Every text of up to 5 letters from `ab`, each with the requirements `""`, `"a"`, `"b"`, `"aa"`, `"ab"` and `"aab"`, 378 calls, against a brute force over every slice: shortest first, then earliest. A requirement the text cannot meet, like `"aab"` in `"ab"`, gives `None`.

The first call is `("", "")`, which must give `(0, 0)`: an empty requirement is met by the empty window, even in an empty text, so check `required` before `text`. Counts matter too: `("aba", "aa")` needs both `a`s, so the answer is the whole text, `(0, 3)`.

KeyError: `owed[c] -= 1` for a character that `required` never mentions, like the `"B"` in `("ABAAC", "AAC")`. Only required characters have entries: check `c in owed` before touching a count, both when `right` takes a character in and when `left` gives one back.
TypeError: `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` comes from reading `best[1] - best[0]` while `best` is still `None`, at the first covering window. Test `best is None` first, in the same condition.
`object of type 'NoneType' has no len()` is `("abc", None)` reaching `len(required)`. That call must raise `ValueError`: check both arguments with `isinstance(..., str)` before anything else.
ValueError: A `ValueError` from `min()` means no slice covered `required`, as in `("ab", "aa")`, so `min` was given nothing to choose from. That case must return `None`.

stopped: The shrinking loop `while missing == 0:` ends only when giving back `text[left]` makes a copy owed again. `left` must move forward on every turn; if it does not, a character that is not required is looked at forever.

If it stopped on a long input of your own, look for work repeated per window: counting every slice from scratch is cubic, and growing a window again from every start is quadratic. The two-pointer scan moves `left` and `right` forward only, so each character enters once and leaves once.
passing: All passing. As your own input, try `minimum_covering_window("ab" * 10000 + "c", "abc")`: the answer is the last three characters, `(19998, 20001)`, and each character enters and leaves the window once, so the time stays small. Then the README's first follow-up: what breaks if `required` must appear in that order?
